study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Kim et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Mapping cerebellar anatomical heterogeneity in mental and neurological illnesses

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping (sinarcsinsh transformation) implemented in PCNtoolkit.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We employed a Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping approach, specifically using the 'sinarcsinsh' transformation.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Cerebellar lobular volumes and voxel-wise gray matter probability values (intensity).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Cerebellar morphology was quantified as lobular volumes or voxel-wise gray matter probability values (multiplied by the Jacobian of the transformation matrix to preserve volumetric information after normalization; see Methods and Supplementary Figs. 2 and 3 for details).
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Kim2023.pdf.md: Results / Lifespan trajectories of cerebellar morphology

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex covariates; scanning site treated as fixed effect (site-related variability correction).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: All normative models included age and sex as covariates, while controlling for scanning-site-related variability. To account for scanner effects, we treated the scanning site as a fixed effect in our analysis.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Kim2023.pdf.md: Results / Lifespan trajectories of cerebellar morphology; Kim2023.pdf.md: Methods
